# Psalm 108 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A-song. A-psalm of-David. Steady my-heart O-God; I-will-sing and-I-will-make-music, also my-glory.

**2** Awake O-harp and-lyre; I-will-awaken the-dawn.

**3** I-will-give-thanks-to-you among-the-peoples O-YHWH, and-I-will-sing-praises-to-you among-the-nations.

**4** For great above the-heavens your-steadfast-love, and-to the-clouds your-faithfulness.

**5** Be-exalted above the-heavens O-God, and-above all the-earth your-glory.

**6** So-that may-be-delivered your-beloved-ones, save with-your-right-hand and-answer-me.

**7** God has-spoken in-his-holiness: 'I-will-exult; I-will-divide Shechem, and-valley-of Succoth I-will-measure-out.

**8** To-me Gilead, to-me Manasseh, and-Ephraim stronghold-of my-head; Judah my-scepter.

**9** Moab my-washbasin; over Edom I-will-throw my-sandal; over Philistia I-will-shout-in-triumph.'

**10** Who will-bring-me to-the-city fortified? Who will-lead-me to Edom?

**11** Have-not you O-God rejected-us? And-you-do-not go-out O-God with-our-armies?

**12** Give to-us help from-distress, and-vain the-salvation-of man.

**13** In-God we-will-do valiantly, and-he will-tread-down our-adversaries.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **108:1-5**: Identical to Psalm 57:7-11; vv. 6-13 identical to Psalm 60:5-12. A composite psalm joining two earlier Davidic fragments.

— EMET
